text:
Recent research supports validating diagnostics with deliberately seeded faults before trusting explanations. [MDPMorph (2025)](https://valerio-terragni.github.io/assets/pdf/li-ase-2025.pdf) combines metamorphic relations with mutated models and measures mutant detection; [statistical metamorphic testing (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11888866/) addresses stochastic neural-network behavior and evaluates tests through mutation testing. These establish useful methods, but do not demonstrate that this recommender toolkit detects padding, leakage, checkpoint, or hook failures. No toolkit-specific detection rates or false-alarm measurements were established by this search.

For BERT4Rec, the [replicability study](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/275645/2/275645.pdf) confirms masked-item training and appended-mask inference; bidirectional shifted-target training can expose answers. Suggested temporary fixtures: unequal-length left-padded histories with known final-position outputs; masked targets checked for accidental visibility; deliberately stale exported weights compared against current-model scores; disabled hooks checked through invocation counters; candidate permutations checked for item-aligned score and ranking consistency. Padding invariance requires preserving valid-token position semantics. [PyTorch documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.Module.html) warns that directly calling `forward` bypasses registered hooks; [assert_close](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing) supports numerical parity checks with explicit tolerances.

Recommended measurement protocol, inferred from these methods: run clean controls and one injected fault at a time; report detected/eligible mutants per fault class and false alarms/clean controls, with denominators and uncertainty. Execute probes independently and record exceptions, missing dependencies, skipped probes, and actual hook calls. A missing SciPy import or failed patch must remain an execution failure, never a successful diagnostic or evidence of model behavior. Simple counts and standard-library confidence intervals can keep this validation dependency-light.
